about: What the port of Ratchet & Clank does differently from the PS2 game. Read by the port's build (port/cmake/Differences.cmake: the Game fixes settings) and the launcher (launcher/core/src/differences.rs: a game's Differences from the original). docs/port/SETTINGS.md section 8 says how to add an entry.

differences.name: Wide-screen effects
differences.original: The game marks a moby drawn only when it is inside its 4:3 picture, and many mobys make their glows, sparkles and particles only while drawn.
differences.port: In a picture wider than 4:3 the port draws the world out to the picture's sides, so mobys there count as drawn too and keep their effects. Off: the console's 4:3 test, and crates, bolts and other mobys near the sides of a wide picture lose their effects.

differences.name: Wide-screen crate orbs
differences.original: The glowing orb on a nanotech crate is a moby of its own, which draws itself only while its centre is inside the game's 4:3 view.
differences.port: The orb's view test sees the wider picture, so nanotech crates at the sides of a wide picture keep their orb. Off: the orbs go out between the 4:3 edge and the picture's.

differences.name: Wide-screen seas, lava
differences.original: Seas, lava and the sand sea (and the other layers the level's draw callbacks send) are culled against the game's 4:3 view.
differences.port: Those callbacks cull against the wider picture, so their tiles reach its sides. Off: the console's 4:3 culling, and tiles near the sides of a wide picture are missing.

differences.name: Cutscenes with a full moby pool
differences.original: When a cutscene starts while the level's 255 moby slots are full (on Gaspar the falling rocks' lava sparks can fill them as the Pilot's Helmet's scene starts), the scene's actor cannot be made and the game reads through the missing moby. On a PS2 that read lands in readable memory and the game most likely carries on unnoticed.
differences.port: On a PC the same read crashes the game, so the port skips that actor: the scene plays without it, and the log says "scene actor skipped". The port's bigger pool (More room for effects) makes this rare; the guard stays for a pool that still fills.

differences.name: More room for effects
differences.original: Each level has 255 slots for the mobys the game makes as it plays (sparks, debris, bolts, enemies a spawner sends). Busy effects can fill them: Gaspar's lava sparks reach 254. A full pool makes the game drop new ones, and a few callers read through the missing moby.
differences.port: More room for effects than on a PS2: the port gives each level 767 slots, so effects and the enemies mods add fit beside each other. Rilgar, Blarg Station and Quartu keep 255, since their memory has no room for more. The tick's list of mobys to target keeps the console's 511 entries, where the game would write past it with more.

differences.name: 60 Hz on the PAL disc
differences.original: The PAL game runs at 50 Hz, with a 60 Hz mode in its Video options for televisions that show it; the mode also sets the game's time base.
differences.port: The port keeps the PAL game in its own 60 Hz mode, as choosing 60 Hz in its menu would, and leaves the row out: a PC display has no 50 Hz television mode, and every disc runs on the same time base.

differences.name: Frames between ticks
differences.port: The game still ticks at its own rate, but the port also draws frames between ticks, with the camera, the mobys and their poses moved from one tick to the next, at the display's rate or the Frame rate setting's. Frame rate Original draws one a tick.
refs: docs/port/SETTINGS.md (2. The tick and the frames)

differences.name: Wider pictures
differences.port: The Picture setting makes it wider (16:10, 16:9, 21:9 and others): the vertical field of view stays the game's and more of the world shows at the sides. 4:3 by default.

differences.name: Plays in the background
differences.original: A console game has the screen and the controller to itself.
differences.port: The game keeps running, and a controller keeps playing it, while another window has the focus; on Windows a full-screen game stays up instead of minimising. The keyboard counts only while the game's window has the focus, and Mute in background silences it.

differences.name: Start skips cutscenes
differences.original: Start alone skips a scene only on Veldin once it is beaten, or in a replay; elsewhere Start needs L1, L2, R1 and R2 held with it.
differences.port: With the Skip cutscenes setting on (the default), Start alone skips an in-game scene: the port holds the four shoulder buttons for it, so the game's own skip ends the scene.

differences.name: Remembered language and sound
differences.original: The language comes from the console's own setting, and the Sound page (playback mode, music and sound volume) resets at power off; loading a save takes the options stored in it.
differences.port: The port keeps the language and the Sound page in its settings file and puts them back at every start. Loading a save keeps the player's options instead of the save's.
